newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Strikes cost S.Korea $3.33 bln in lost output.
newsitem.headline: Strikes cost S.Korea $3.33 bln in lost output.

text.p: South Korean production losses from recent labour strikes are expected to hit 2.85 trillion won ($3.33 billion) by the end of Wednesday, a trade ministry official said.
He said lost exports from the industrial action that began on December 26 after the forced passage of a controversial labour law would be at $509 million.
Key sectors of South Korea's export-led economy have been hit by more than three weeks of wildcat stoppages.
An outlawed union directing most of the industrial action has since decided to limit strikes, opting to hold weekly stoppages on Wednesdays.
But workers responded only half-heartedly on Wednesday to the strike call by the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions following President Kim Young-sam's stunning retreat over the labour law.
On Tuesday Kim agreed to send the law back to parliament for debate.
